purpose: Prefer high-signal optional subject-matter sources for emulator installation, networking, content identity, source navigation, collection management, and troubleshooting. Sources advise; no single source is mandatory.

trust_levels.official: Primary project/vendor source. Prefer for binaries, releases, setup, networking, and project-specific behavior.
trust_levels.reference: Specialized preservation/identity database. Prefer for hashes, media identity, release metadata, and dump verification.
trust_levels.community: Useful community-maintained technical knowledge, navigation, or established archive. Cross-check important identity claims against reference data when possible.
trust_levels.secondary: Helpful supplemental reference, but freshness/completeness can vary. Never prefer over an official upstream source for emulator/tool binaries.

expert_roles.runtime-authority: Authoritative source for an emulator/tool's current release and behavior.
expert_roles.source-navigator: Helps locate established collections or useful source paths.
expert_roles.content-archive: Established archive that may directly carry classic-game content.
expert_roles.firmware-specialist: Tracks BIOS/firmware requirements, files, hashes, and emulator expectations.
expert_roles.identity-verifier: Verifies content identity, region, revision, tracks, and hashes.
expert_roles.collection-manager: Organizes, identifies, filters, patches, or reports on a local game collection.
expert_roles.transport-authority: Authoritative source for multiplayer transport/network behavior.

sources.name: DuckStation
sources.use_for: PS1 emulator downloads and authoritative DuckStation behavior. Prefer this over third-party DuckStation installers or repacks.

sources.name: PCSX2
sources.use_for: PS2 emulator downloads, stable/nightly guidance, and setup documentation.

sources.name: Dolphin Emulator
sources.use_for: GameCube/Wii emulator downloads, controller configuration, ripping/dumping documentation, and NetPlay requirements.

sources.name: xemu
sources.use_for: Original Xbox emulator downloads and authoritative xemu networking/System Link behavior.

sources.name: Libretro Documentation
sources.use_for: RetroArch/core documentation and constraints. Use project/core-specific documentation before assuming every system supports reliable netplay.

sources.name: Flycast Dojo
sources.use_for: Flycast Dojo releases, match-code/P2P setup, file parity, and Dojo-specific troubleshooting.

sources.name: Parsec Support
sources.use_for: Remote-couch controller passthrough, streaming, and guest gamepad troubleshooting.

sources.name: XLink Kai
sources.use_for: Supported System Link/LAN titles, Kai setup, and xemu integration.

sources.name: Redump
sources.use_for: Optical-disc identity and checksum comparison: region, revision, track layout, and bad-dump investigation. Treat Redump primarily as verification/reference data, not as the source of the game bytes.

sources.name: r/Roms Megathread
sources.use_for: Community-maintained navigation to preservation-oriented collections and BIOS sets. Prefer named Redump/No-Intro collections and verify important content against the corresponding reference database.

sources.name: RetroBIOS
sources.use_for: BIOS/firmware discovery and emulator-oriented verification. The project derives file requirements from emulator/platform source and records multiple fingerprints. Use it as a firmware specialist; do not treat its firmware hashes as a substitute for game-disc identity databases.

sources.name: Vimm's Lair
sources.status_note: Long-running community archive. Availability is incomplete because some publishers have requested removal of titles. Confirm the exact vimm.net domain and do not assume similarly named domains are affiliated.
sources.use_for: Established classic-game archive/source when a title is still present. Generally preferable to random search-result ROM sites; verify disc identity against Redump when it matters. Do not use Vimm-hosted emulator binaries in preference to the emulator project's current official release.

sources.name: Internet Archive
sources.use_for: Reputable archival hosting infrastructure used by many preservation collections. Trust is collection-specific: prefer collections identified by Redump/No-Intro/TOSEC metadata or reached through a curated index, and verify bytes when identity matters.

sources.name: No-Intro DAT-o-MATIC
sources.use_for: Cartridge-oriented release identity and checksum metadata.

sources.name: Igir
sources.use_for: Manage a local ROM/disc-image collection: scan against DATs, identify and rename files, filter duplicates/regions, patch, create playlists, and report missing or unknown content. It manages player-owned/local bytes; it is not a content source.

sources.name: ConsoleMods Wiki
sources.use_for: Community-maintained console hardware, repair, preservation, and dumping knowledge. Cross-check risky hardware/modification steps and heed page warnings.

sources.name: Emulation General Wiki
sources.use_for: Broad community orientation and emulator comparisons. Follow through to the emulator's own upstream site before downloading binaries.

sources.name: PCGamingWiki - Emulation
sources.use_for: Supplemental PC-side troubleshooting and configuration context. Verify freshness against current upstream documentation.

sources.name: Microsoft PowerShell Get-FileHash
sources.use_for: Compute local file hashes before comparing a download, emulator binary, archive, or game image against a trusted published identity.

rules: Sources are optional subject-matter experts, not mandatory dependencies. Consult the smallest relevant set for the current question.
For emulator binaries, prefer the emulator project's official website/repository/release page over mirrors or aggregators.
Do not require the player to prove provenance before helping with identity, integrity, source reputation, compatibility, configuration, or troubleshooting.
When a player needs a file, name useful reputable sources or source indexes and explain what each is trustworthy for rather than stopping at 'obtain the file'.
A matching filename is weak evidence; hashes and expected archive/image structure are stronger identity signals.
A clean antivirus result is not proof of safety. Prefer trustworthy source paths plus hashes/signatures when available and sensible file structure.
Community archives and indexes can be useful without being authoritative. Distinguish source reputation, collection provenance, and byte-level verification.
Community wikis are useful orientation, not authority over an emulator project's current release documentation.
If a page tells the player to disable antivirus, install a browser extension/download manager, or run an unrelated executable to obtain a data image/archive, treat it as high risk.
